chunks.text:
ELECTRICAL& ELECTRONICS ENGINEERING
Department Vision and Mission
To produce globally competitive engineering graduates and become center of excellence through research in the areas of Electrical & Electronics Engineering.
To impart quality and contemporary education in the realm of Electrical & electronics engineering.
To pursue research and new technologies in Electrical & Electronics Engineering and related disciplines in order to serve the needs of the society.
Department of  Electrical & Electronics Engineering
The Department of
Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE)
focuses on the
study of electrical systems, electronics, power generation, distribution, and control, as well as renewable energy technologies and advanced automation systems.
It provides students with a strong foundation in
Electrical Machines, Power Systems, Control Systems, Power Electronics, Renewable Energy, and Embedded Systems
, enabling them to address diverse engineering challenges.
The curriculum combines theoretical principles with practical implementation through hands-on lab sessions, projects, and design simulations, preparing students to develop and manage efficient electrical and electronic systems.
The program emphasizes practical learning through advanced labs like
Power Electronics Drives Lab, Electrical Machines Lab, and Simulation Lab,
offering students the tools to innovate and solve real-world problems.
Research and Innovation Opportunities: The department collaborates with power sector companies, automation industries, and research institutions, offering students opportunities for internships, live projects, and industry-relevant problem-solving.
Career Development Support: Dedicated career counseling, workshops, and placement assistance prepare students for competitive exams, interviews, and industry roles, ensuring strong placement outcomes and pathways for academic and professional growth.
Faculty

chunks.heading: Basic Electrical Engineering Lab:
chunks.text:
Basic Electrical Engineering Lab:
The Basic Electrical Engineering Lab introduces foundational concepts of electrical engineering in an engaging, practical setting.
Featuring essential equipment for studying simple circuits, electrical machines, and measurement techniques, the lab serves as a stepping stone for all engineering disciplines to understand the basics of power, energy, and electrical safety.

chunks.heading: Electrical Circuits Lab:
chunks.text:
Electrical Circuits Lab:
The Electrical Circuits Lab is a state-of-the-art facility for studying the behavior of electrical circuits.
Equipped with tools for analyzing both AC and DC circuits, it allows students to verify network theorems, study transient and steady-state responses, and explore resonance.
The lab promotes a hands-on approach to circuit design and analysis using simulation and real-time hardware.

chunks.heading: Electrical Machines-I Lab:
chunks.text:
Electrical Machines-I Lab:
The Electrical Machines-I Lab is a hands-on learning facility that provides students with an opportunity to explore the fundamentals of DC machines and transformers.
Equipped with modern testing instruments and high-quality machines, the lab allows students to study machine characteristics, efficiency, and performance under various load conditions, fostering a deep understanding of electromechanical energy conversion.

chunks.heading: Electrical Machines-II Lab:
chunks.text:
Electrical Machines-II Lab:
The Electrical Machines-II Lab is a well-equipped setup designed for in-depth exploration of AC machines, including induction motors and synchronous machines.
With advanced measuring instruments and modern machine models, the lab enables students to conduct performance tests, synchronization experiments, and speed control techniques, preparing them for industrial applications.

chunks.heading: Electrical Measurements and Instrumentation Lab:
chunks.text:
Electrical Measurements and Instrumentation Lab:
The Electrical Measurements Lab is a precision-oriented space focused on teaching students the principles of accurate measurement and instrumentation.
It features calibrated devices such as ammeters, voltmeters, wattmeters, and energy meters.
Students gain practical knowledge in measuring electrical quantities, calibrating instruments, and minimizing errors, essential for reliable engineering solutions.

chunks.heading: Linear Control Systems Lab:
chunks.text:
Linear Control Systems Lab:
The Control Systems Lab provides a practical environment for studying feedback systems and control principles.
Equipped with advanced tools like programmable logic controllers (PLCs) and MATLAB/Simulink, the lab allows students to design, analyze, and implement controllers for stability and performance enhancement in real-world systems.

chunks.heading: Power Electronics and Drives Lab:
chunks.text:
Power Electronics and Drives Lab:
The Power Electronics Drives Lab offers a cutting-edge platform to explore the integration of power electronics with motor drives.
Featuring devices like IGBTs, MOSFETs, and programmable power converters, the lab enables students to experiment with speed control of AC and DC motors and understand energy-efficient drive systems for industrial applications.

chunks.heading: Electrical Design and Simulation Lab:
chunks.text:
Electrical Design and Simulation Lab:
The Electrical Design and Simulation Lab is a comprehensive facility designed to provide students with hands-on experience in advanced computational tools and software.

chunks.heading: This lab is divided into three specialized areas:
chunks.text:
This lab is divided into three specialized areas:
i) Computer-Aided Electrical Design Lab: Equipped with industry-standard software such as Microsoft VISIO and AUTOCAD, this section enables students to create precise electrical drawings, layouts, and schematics for real-world applications.
ii) Power Systems Simulation Lab: Utilizing MATLAB/Simulink and PSIM, this area allows students to simulate and analyze power system components, enabling them to study power flow, fault analysis, and dynamic behavior under various conditions.
iii) Electrical Circuit Simulation Lab: Focused on modeling and simulating electrical circuits and systems using MATLAB/Simulink, this section helps students understand steady-state and transient responses, optimize system performance, and explore control strategies for electrical networks.
